title: scan.rs parse_begin_line rejects empty filename; decode.rs accepts it — API inconsistency causes scan to miss blocks decode handles
description:
uuencoding/src/scan.rs parse_begin_line() returns None when filename_bytes is empty (line 83-85), so scan() silently drops blocks with empty filenames. But uuencoding/src/decode.rs decode() accepts 'begin 644 ' (empty filename) and returns a DecodedBlock with filename=''. The two code paths disagree on what is valid. A real-world email with 'begin 644 
...
end
' will: succeed through decode(), but be silently skipped by scan(). Callers relying on scan() to find all blocks will miss these.
acceptance_criteria: Align scan.rs: accept an empty filename (return a BlockMetadata with filename=''), matching decode.rs behavior. Add a test in scan.rs for an empty-filename begin line.
close_reason: Removed empty-filename guard in parse_begin_line; added test
